He is the most precious little bundle of joy, and our hearts are full of happiness and gratitude,” they wrote in a joint statement. “He is a big, strong, sweet guy, and he already has quite the personality. We are so excited to show him the world and bring him along for the ride!” The Bravo stars also thanked the staff at Lenox Hill Hospital in New York City for helping them welcome Leo into the world. “A special thank you to the amazing doctors and nurses at Lennox Hill for taking such great care of us,” they wrote. “We are forever grateful! ❤️” The new parents received plenty of love from their Summer House and In the City franchise family in the comments section of their Instagram post. “He is so freaking cute,” Ciara Miller beamed. The Challenge alum Nicole Zanatta welcomed twin daughters Seraphina and Madyson on May 1.  “Becoming their mom has been the greatest blessing of my life, but our journey hasn’t been easy,” Zanatta wrote via Instagram on June 1. “Both of my girls were diagnosed with congenital CMV (Cytomegalovirus), a virus I had never heard of until it became part of our story.” She continued, “Since birth, we’ve spent time in the NICU, attended countless appointments which are still ongoing, undergone testing and started medications. I recently brought them home a week ago, but our journey is far from over. Through every high and low, I choose faith over fear, resilience over doubt, and gratitude for every blessing along the way. I will give my girls every opportunity to thrive. I will always fight for them and advocate for their needs.” According to the Mayo Clinic, CMV is "a condition caused by a common virus.” The CMV virus stays in the body for life once a person is infected and can spread through body fluids, including blood, saliva, urine, semen and breast milk.

#3757. GTA 6 Has Sold Almost 8 Million Copies So Far, And PS5 Is Dominating The Split (Of Course)

The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 7.71 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $751 million in gross revenue.

The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 5.74 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 1.97 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 7.71 million GTA 6 sales so far, 74% are on PS5 and 26% on Xbox Series X|S.

In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $559 million in revenue, compared to $192 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies.

The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market.

Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and if the 74/26 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S.

Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator.

Circana has released new data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game.

GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted issues, experts believe.

The Star Wars movies are some of the most iconic films of all time, with generations of moviegoers growing up on the galaxy far, far away in theaters and streaming with a Disney+ subscription. Still, the franchise isn't without criticism, coming from both fans and naysayers. Case in point: Project Hail Mary writer Andy Weir recently spoke about the space opera, and the "problem" that exists in that world. To be honest, I see his point.

Project Hail Mary crushed in theaters earlier this year, and the book to screen adaptation is now available to stream with an Amazon Prime subscription. During a recent interview with Slash Film, Weir was asked what he'd do with Star Wars if he could, responding with:

Star Wars is more about massive upheaval. One problem that happens is, if you're going to have a story about a monumental war, then when it's over and the good guys win, you want it to stay that way. So it's very unsatisfying if you roll into a new monumental war.

Honestly, points were made. The original Star Wars trilogy focused on the Rebels fighting against the Galactic Empire, which ended in a big way during Return of the Jedi. Unfortunately, this conflict was followed basically beat for beat during the sequel trilogy. In those films it was the Resistance who was fighting agains the evil First Order. And yes, the bad guys had planet-destroying tech at their disposal in both.

This is an issue a number of fans have taken with the sequel trilogy, including Oscar Isaac's viral line about Palpatine returning. So what should the franchise have done instead of focusing on yet another giant space war? In the same interview Andy Weir offered some insight, saying:

Think of it like this: We know what happened in World War II, but there are some really good fictional stories that take place during World War II. So if you treat the Galactic Civil War as, 'Okay, that's established canon, those are the things that happened,' but there's still a lot of stories to tell about other people living through those wars. So that's what I would do.

Sign me up. Weir knows what he'd do with upcoming Star Wars movies and TV shows, we'll just have to see if the powers that be at Lucasfilm agree. There are a number of thrilling projects coming down the line, including Shawn Levy's Starfighter movie. That movie seems like it'll be a much more capsulated story, which might be the type of story that Weir would appreciate.

Star Wars: Starfighter will hit theaters on May 28th, 2027. While we wait, fans can re-watch the franchise on Disney+, or Project Hail Mary over on Amazon. The latter might have a chance at some nominations during Awards Season, so the pressure is on.

#3754. Nintendo Could Have A New Cartridge Problem On Its Hands

As PlayStation prepares to embrace an all-digital future starting in 2028, Nintendo is seen as one of the last bastions of physical games with its Switch cartridges. A new challenge has emerged: one of Nintendo's major ROM chip manufacturers, Macronix, is preparing to exit the market and shift its focus to the more lucrative flash and memory chip market.

In its latest earnings call (via MST Financial analyst David Gibson), Macronix revealed it plans to drop ROM manufacturing entirely. The company says ROM chips account for only 5% of its business, down from 26% a year ago. While Macronix isn't the only company that manufactures ROM chips for Nintendo, it is a major supplier overall, and losing it could put further pressure on the company and other game publishers to ship more games on Game-Key Cards, or increase prices for cartridges that do have full games installed.

ROM chips--which stand for Read-Only Memory--are specialized storage chips that data is permanently written to. The great thing about them is that they let games load quickly, since a console can read the game code straight off the chip without first installing data to an internal storage drive. Nintendo's proprietary game cards rely on specialized, high-speed ROM tech tailored specifically for Nintendo hardware.

Because of that design, they have high manufacturing costs and only a handful of silicon suppliers--including MegaChips and ROHM--manufacture them for Nintendo. This, in turn, affects publishers' profit margins, which is why Game-Key Cards on Switch 2 are a popular alternative. In comparison, they act as digital authentication keys that require a game to be downloaded directly to the Switch 2 flash storage.

We have reached out to Nintendo, and will update this post if we hear back from them.

The rise of AI companies has also had an impact on virtually every aspect of consoles, and memory is no exception, as prices have risen dramatically over the last two years. Several tech companies have also shifted from selling products to consumers to selling exclusively to AI companies, which have an incredible appetite for memory and storage. That pivot has proven lucrative, as all the RAM for 2027 looks to be sold out already.

For its part, Nintendo says it doesn't plan to abandon physical games yet, as it prefers to offer consumers an "agnostic" platform to play games on.

Ohio was home to one of the nation’s most competitive races for governor in the 2026 midterm elections, as entrepreneur and former Republican presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy and Democrat physician Amy Acton battled to replace term-limited GOP governor Mike DeWine. #3752. Former Halo Composer Marty O’Donnell Loses Congressional Race In Nevada

One of the minds behind the legendary music of Halo fell short in his mission to pivot to politics. Marty O'Donnell, formerly a composer and audio director for Bungie, lost his bid to join the U.S. House of Representatives by a wide margin.

With 86% of votes counted, AP News called the race in Nevada's 3rd congressional district for incumbent Representative Susie Lee, a Democrat. O'Donnell ran as a Republican and had the endorsement of President Donald Trump. The current count has O'Donnell with 38.6% of the vote, trailing Lee's 59.1%. Nevada's 3rd district includes much of Clark County and part of Las Vegas.

Lee, who has held her seat since 2019, has been a target of Republicans in previous election cycles. As it became clear early Wednesday morning that Lee was favored to win re-election, her social media account posted the famous "Halo theme song performed by 80 guys in 1 bathroom" video to mock O'Donnell. O'Donnell responded by saying in a post: "Susie has a lot of class. And it’s all low."

O'Donnell heavily leaned on his video game industry background, hosting a campaign event that doubled as a celebration of early Halo games. At the event, O'Donnell declared that "gamers are not woke" and insisted that games, movies, and comics were "co-opted by left-wing politics."

As Lee's social media video hints at, this wasn't O'Donnell's first attempt at entering national politics. O'Donnell ran for the same congressional seat in 2024, placing fourth in the Republican primary. He won the Republican nomination in 2026 with the backing of Trump.

O'Donnell began his career in video game music composition as a freelancer, producing the music for Bungie's Myth and Myth 2. He joined Bungie as a full-time employee starting with 2001's Oni and went on to compose music for all of Bungie's Halo titles and the first Destiny game. O'Donnell was fired from Bungie in 2014; the composer claimed that he was terminated "without cause" and pursued legal action against the company afterward. According to his campaign website, O'Donnell is now retired from the game industry.

#3749. Is The Gears Of War Movie Actually Going To Happen? Director Weighs In

A Gears of War movie is in development at Netflix, but is it ever going to happen? That remains to be seen, but director David Leitch of John Wick fame recently said the movie will "hopefully" come to fruition "soon."

Speaking to ScreenRant, Leitch said, "I think everybody's excited about the potential of this as a film universe."

He added: "I wish I could tell you more, because there's some much cool stuff going on."

Netflix recently underwent a big shift in management, with film chief Dan Lin exiting the company alongside longtime chief content officer Bela Bajaria. Former Former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice is now the new chief content officer. He was only just recently installed in the post, so it remains to be seen what changes Rice could make. There is, however, precedent for new management making big changes, as Netflix's BioShock movie was scaled back under the leadership of Lin.

The latest script for the Gears of War movie as of 2025 was written by Jon Spaihts, who previously wrote Prometheus, Doctor Strange, and Passengers, along with Dune 1 and 2.

A decades-long wait

Gears of War fans have been waiting decades for their promised Gears of War movie. All the way back in 2007, a year after the first Gears of War game came out, New Line Cinema purchased the rights to make a movie based on the game. Nothing ever came of that. Then in 2016, the Gears of War movie rights changed hands and went to Universal. Nothing came of that, either.

In 2022, Netflix announced a deal with Microsoft to make not only a Gears of War movie, but also an animated TV series (which we don’t know anything about). It’s been four years since then and the project remains in development, but things tend to fall apart in Hollywood, so there are no guarantees it’ll actually happen.

Netflix is also working on an Assassin’s Creed TV show, and that one is actually going to happen, as it is now filming. Additionally, Netflix is behind the BioShock movie from The Hunger Games director Francis Lawrence, and it’s set to begin production in 2027.

Who could be in the Gears of War movie?

Wrestler-turned-actor Dave Bautista has lobbied for years to play Marcus, and he does bear a strong resemblance to the character, but no casting announcements for the Gears of War movie have been made. He's already involved in a big video game project, as he's starring as Kratos in Prime Video's God of War show. Meanwhile, Gears of War designer Cliff Bleszinski has previously been adamant that Chris Pratt shouldn’t play any role in the film.

What about the Gears of War games?

The latest entry in the game series was this year's Gears of War: E-Day, a highly regarded action game that reportedly has not sold very well. No new games in the series have been announced, but developer The Coalition has said it won't take another seven years to make a follow-up.

Zooming further out, Xbox is undergoing a major "reset" that has included mass layoffs, game cancellations, and studio closures/divestitures. Developers at The Coalition said they fear for their jobs.

#3745. Jodie Sweetin Learned 'Humility' After Having to 'Put S*** Back' at Target

Jodie Sweetin has reaped the benefits of fame, but during her lowest of lows, she was barely making ends meet.

“[It’s] not like I was ever a materialistic person,” Sweetin, 44, said during the Wednesday, November 4, episode of the “We’re Still Here, Babe” podcast. “But you learn humility when you are at Target and you’ve got to turn around and go, you know, put some s*** back, ‘cause you don’t have the money on your debit card.”

The actress recalled that after finding success as Stephanie Tanner on Full House from 1987 to 1995, she had to face her drug and alcohol addiction head on. Sweetin got sober in 2011, but soon realized that the money she had from the hit sitcom was “gone” so she started working as a logistics coordinator at a treatment center in Los Angeles.

It was during that time, Sweetin said she learned a lot about herself and what she could achieve outside of acting.

“I was happy. I think part of the reason I was able to come back into the [entertainment] business and enjoy it truly was is that I had gone completely in the other direction,” she recalled. “I was working a normal job.”

The Hallmark actress noted that she “had no money” while working at the treatment center and raising her two daughters, Zoie, 18, and Beatrix, 16, as a single mom. (Sweetin shares Zoie with second husband Cody Herpin and Beatrix with third husband Morty Coyle.)

“I lived in a one and a half bedroom apartment with the kids,” Sweetin recalled. “I was making like $2,200 a month and my parents were paying half my rent. I was just trying to get by. Drove an old used car.”

The former child star, who married her fourth husband, Mescal Wasilewski, in 2022, revealed that she chose to look at her “normal job” as a blessing.

“I didn’t have [an] ego about it,” Sweetin explained. “I didn’t care that I was quote, unquote, working a normal job. I think other people again were like, ‘What are you doing here?’ And I was like, ‘Paying my bills. Kids don’t pay for themselves.’”

The Jane Mysteries star ultimately learned to embrace life outside of the spotlight, admitting, “I was like, I would be fine doing this if this is what I’m going to do, cool. And I just threw myself into being as fully present as I could be and that old you know ‘bloom where you’re planted’ kind of vibe.”

Sweetin continued, “Like, if this is what it is, then I’m going to make it good, and I’m going to have fun, and I’m going to enjoy it.”

She added that with time she “learned to be really happy and I loved my life.”

Sweetin noted, “I have had and I have definitely not had, and I’ve learned to exist in both. Now does money make certain problems much easier, yes. Does it make other things much harder? Yes.”

Because of her positive headspace, Sweetin said she was “good” with the idea of never acting again but her luck changed when Netflix’s Fuller House was greenlit.

“I was very much straddling that line while pitching the show,” Sweetin said of her financial insecurity ahead of the show’s 2016 premiere. (Fuller House ran from 2016 to 2020 and followed Stephanie Tanner and big sister D.J. Tanner, played by Candace Cameron Bure, and their lives as adults.)

In fact, her situation was quite scary before she started seeing a consistent paycheck.

“I had to borrow money the first week I was working on Fuller House and I skidded into my first paycheck with like $190 in my bank account,” Sweetin recalled. “And nobody that I worked with knew that. Not that I cared.”

Looking back, she said, “I’ve been very fortunate to know a lot of really wonderful things,” but when times get tough, “your ego can’t be involved in it.”

#3744. Nexus Mods Won’t Ban AI Mods, But It Won’t Let Them Hide Either

Nexus Mods owner Victor "Foledinho" Folmann has outlined plans to make AI disclosures mandatory for PC mods uploaded to the site. While content built with AI tools won't be banned--despite it being a contentious subject in the modding community--Folmann did reveal that Nexus Mods will ultimately require modders to clearly communicate when AI has been used.

"We already have tags for AI-generated and AI-assisted mods, but we recognize that there’s a lot more we can do to make that information more accessible and clear for you all," Folmann wrote. "As of today, we're making AI disclosure mandatory when uploading a new mod, meaning mod authors will need to declare whether AI has been used in their work. All existing mods will have one of two popups: a persistent one when editing a mod in the upload form, and a dismissible one on the 'My Mods' page."

At the same time, Nexus Mods users will be able to filter out AI-produced mods entirely from their search results, similar to what Itch.io does as part of its efforts to combat AI spam uploads. As for why Nexus Mods will allow AI content to remain on the site, Folmann added that an outright ban would likely lead modders to simply not declare their use of AI tools in their mod-creation-efforts. By allowing and moderating it, the site can motivate users to be more transparent.

"An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process but will prevent people from mentioning its use. We'd prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform," Folmann wrote. "Mod authors should have a chance to decide about the further use of their work, and you should be able to decide for yourselves how much AI-based content you want to see, whether more, less, or no content at all."

Nexus Mods' official stance is that it will not use mods to train AI, nor will it sell or license them out, Folmann added. The site will continue to fine-tune its approach to AI-assisted mods while also punishing anyone caught breaking its new disclosure rules.

AI has been a hot-button issue lately for PC gamers, with the recent Steam Next Fest highlighting a growing problem of slop flooding the platform.

Game developers have also reported that the mandatory QA check every game must pass before launch is taking even longer now, with studios blaming a deluge of AI-generated games for slowing down the process. This week, Steam announced new game submission rules to get things back on track, including requiring developers to ensure their game can run through the Steam Client for at least five minutes before they hit the submit key.

The Scene In You Can See Everything That Showed EVERYTHING Might NOT Have Been Billy Evans' Idea

Nathan Fielder Spoke To Elizabeth Holmes From Prison Just Prior To Doc Release. What She Told Him Fascinates Me

What does Holmes’ unblinking stare tell us?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Amateur psychologists across the internet are still trying to make sense of everything they saw in You Can See Everything. The box office hit has been the talk of the 2026 movie schedule this fall, with audiences weighing in on former Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, and the discussion is all over the place, from former co-workers to Holmes' partner, Billy Evans. Recently, an outlet even sat down with three actual psychologists to get their opinions on what they see (and don’t see) in the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim-directed film.

As the Boston Globe makes clear, these are the psychologists' opinions, though they have never treated Holmes or Evans. Still, the comments are insightful and fascinating. If you’ve seen the movie, you know that “truth” is at the core of the questions being asked by it. Is Holmes lying? Is Evans? Is Fielder? Dr. Matt Jerram, a psychologist at Boston Neuropsychological Services, addressed that:

I still didn’t walk away feeling confident one way or the other whether she lied about everything or not. But I did walk away feeling confident that there was a portrayal of her that was different in each spot. So whether what she was doing in this documentary was the real her versus just another portrayal, it doesn’t matter necessarily. But it was really striking how different the identities were. You have this high-powered woman who’s going to be CEO of the year, and then you have the person who, at least the story is, can’t stand up for herself in any relationship, right?

There is a striking difference between Holmes at the height of her acclaim, before the house of cards collapsed and she was sent to prison for fraud, and the Holmes we meet in the movie. One of the major differences we see is in her relationship with Evans, as Dr. Jerram mentioned. Dr. Kristina Pinto, another psychologist at Boston Neuropsychological Services, also talked about that:

Relationships are so centrally implicated in personality disorders. What raises the specter of a personality disorder here is just how her identity and personality shift by relationship. The whole scene where she says she’s never lied once, and it’s like, oh well, that’s an interesting personality trait. And then by the end of the movie, she’s saying, ‘Now I don’t have to pretend with Billy, I don’t have to pretend here.’ So this is someone who’s saying to us an hour and a half ago, ‘I don’t lie,’ and then by the end she, at least in the retelling, she’s acknowledging that she has had to pretend.

In a movie that never lets audiences get concrete answers (one of the most brilliant things about this Oscar contender), these things brought up by the psychologists only dig deeper into my bewilderment. That befuddlement is, in large part, due to Holmes, of course. And some of that comes from her unblinking stare that everyone has become so familiar with.

Her eyes were always wide open. Her whole facial expression would tend to draw in people who want to be sympathetic to her. It was kind of childlike in a lot of ways.

Dr. Alice Connors-Kellgren, a psychologist and director of psychology and psychology training at Tufts Medical Center, expanded on that:

I found myself really not connecting with her very much, or having a lot of empathy or sympathy for her. I think because it felt like she got the childlike, ‘I’m gonna pull you in,’ and then she went way too far with it.

So, we’re still left with what and who to believe in You Can See Everything, and we’re also left contemplating just who Elizabeth Holmes is. Is she the master manipulator she was convicted by a court of being, or is she the one being manipulated due to an undiagnosed neurodivergence, as the scene watching “Who’s On First?” tries to argue? Dr. Jerram’s thoughts are interesting:

My feeling was either she is a tremendous actress or, you know, she has actually got some stuff going on. I would want to know a lot more before I drew a final conclusion. I would definitely say she clearly has some difficulty understanding subtext and understanding, say, you know, simile, metaphor, those types of cognition.

So the debate will rage on in the public square, probably at least until the Oscars in March. I’m all for continuing it, because it’s one of the most fascinating films I’ve ever seen. The more I think about it, the better it gets.

Hugh Scott is the Syndication Editor for CinemaBlend. Before CinemaBlend, he was the managing editor for Suggest.com and Gossipcop.com, covering celebrity news and debunking false gossip. He has been in the publishing industry for almost two decades, covering pop culture – movies and TV shows, especially – with a keen interest and love for Gen X culture, the older influences on it, and what it has since inspired. He graduated from Boston University with a degree in Political Science but cured himself of the desire to be a politician almost immediately after graduation.

#3742. God Of War Laufey Delayed

Santa Monica Studios has delayed God of War Laufey. The new God of War game for PS5 is no longer set for release in February 2027, and has shifted to May 2027.

The game will now launch on May 20, 2027, which is a delay of about three months from its original February 16, 2027 release date.

"We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," the developer said. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."

God of War Laufey stars Deborah Ann Woll as Faye. Starring alongside Woll is The Boys actor Jack Quaid, who plays a gelatinous cube named Phranque.

Compared to Kratos and his skillful application of brute force to help solve problems, Faye is far more graceful and nimble. Like the previous games, God of War Laufey is a third-person action experience built around chaining together various skills and weapons to dish out tremendous amounts of damage.

You can see the game in action in the gameplay trailer below.

A new Kratos-led game is coming after that, and it will pick up where Laufey left off.

#3741. It’s Great To Be A Cow In World Of Warcraft: Forever

World of WarcraftWorld of Warcraft: Forever

Ah, Mulgore. The enormous, bright blue skies. The crunch of prairie grass under my hooves. The glorious sunrises and sunsets. The shimmer of Stonebull Lake and the awesome sight of Thunder Bluff’s great plateaus looming in the distance. It’s great to be a tauren!

Every race in World of Warcraft gets a couple of special abilities unique to their people. What these abilities are has varied over the years as the game was rebalanced in various ways. One racial ability that, for years, was never used, was called Plainsrunning. It was an ability unique to the tauren, a race of humanoids with cow-like features. In the original beta version of WoW, tauren were the one race that did not receive mounts to ride on at level 40, likely because they were kind of big and bulky characters that didn’t fit nicely on a horse. Instead, they received a quest to learn plainsrunning, which let them run real fast, equivalent to how fast a mount would move. At some point, it was decided that this wasn’t an amazing idea, the Plainsrunning racial was removed, and tauren were given sick-ass kodos to ride instead.

Plainsrunning was eventually forgotten, becoming nothing more than an interesting historical fragment of data, until very, very recently, when it was reintroduced in WoW: Forever‘s beta. This new version of Plainsrunning worked a little bit differently, and let tauren slowly build up running speed over time as they moved, as long as they didn’t stop or engage in combat. So while not making much difference over short distances, it could theoretically build up and eventually give tauren a real nice top speed for getting around the world, particularly at lower levels.

But then, after the beta shut down and in the weeks before the game actually launched, Blizzard changed something. It freakin’Â buffed Plainsrunning, bringing it to a cap of 60-percent movement speed increase.

Guys, that’sÂ so fast.Â That’s as fast as an apprentice-level mount, which you don’t get until level 40. This is available for tauren at level 1. Tauren right now are zooming across Mulgore. You just see one go by, wa-pow! There and gone in a flash.

Now, granted, it takes some time to build up to 60 percent. You get a stack of Plainsrunning every few seconds, and each stack is worth a 2-percent increase, to a cap of 30 stacks. So you gotta run for a while, unimpeded, without fighting or stopping to pick a Peacebloom, in order to get that sweet, sweet 60 percent. But let me tell you something. Classic WoW? Lotta running. Lotta running long, long distances, across entire zones and continents. In fact, one of the things people love about older versions of World of WarcraftÂ is the slower pace. But Plainsrunning creeps up to max speed so gradually that it gives you the fun of moving quick without detracting from that in any way. Even with all the new fast-travel additions in Forever, you’re still going to be doing a lot of hoofing it, literally if you’re a tauren. So being able to slam that Num Lock down, kick back, and (eventually) go fast? What a dream.

It’s great to be a tauren in WoW: Forever! I’m goingÂ so fastÂ right now. You’ll need a horse to catch this cow.

#3740. As Donald Trump's Handpicked Candidates Flop Nationwide, the President Accepts Reality

As the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections began to roll in, Donald Trump’s mood seemed to darken, especially when it came to coverage from his network of choice, Fox News. But after a few posts complaining about the cable news channel, the president fell silent for hours, before telling the New York Times that he will accept the results of Tuesday's election.

As polls closed in Indiana and Kentucky at 6 p.m. ET, Trump termed the end to the latter state's election day “A BIG DEAL!” The president was likely aware of the closure as he was “Watching the Pre-Election Results on FoxNews,” he wrote, before complaining that he can't stand the voice of one of the network's few liberal leaning commentators, Jessica Tarlov.

“DUMB AS A ROCK,” Trump complained, his mood apparently turning. “Have to go somewhere else until that LOSER is off the air — I'll be back later!” After less than an hour, he returned, his anger at Fox increasing. “The FoxNews Poll, always the worst, is so insulting with the questions they ask,” he wrote. “Every question is a hit job, and every answer is ‘BULLSHIT!’ This has been going on for years.”

A few minutes later, he returned again, this time with a longer rant about the cable channel. “FoxNews Ratings are way down (27%!) because they’re spending too much time covering the Trump Deranged Dumocrats! All of those people who used to watch Fox, and no longer do, get it. It’s them, not me — My numbers are better than they have ever been.”

“No wonder FoxNews Ratings are collapsing, and they’re going to go down a lot further,” he continued. “They’re way down, not because of me, but because they are AGAINST me! This happened once before, and Fox almost collapsed. It’s happening again!”

In Georgia, Trump had earlier stumped for gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson and US Senate nominee Mike Collins, who lost his race against incumbent Democratic senator Jon Ossoff. When that race was called, Trump made no comment. The same was true as Democrat James Talarico's lead over Texas Senate hopeful Ken Paxton continued to grow. Those who checked Truth Social after CNN projected that the Democratic party would capture the House of Representatives were also set up for disappointment, as the president has yet to comment on those results as well.

Instead, he returned some hours later with a post not about any candidate, but his own popularity. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!,” the president wrote. Shortly thereafter, at around 10:30 p.m. ET, the president spoke with the New York Times, where he struck a conciliatory tone. “I am absolutely willing to accept those results,” he told the paper. “We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out.”

And, minutes later, another Truth Social post. “I'm going to become a Political Pundit, both good and bad, on the reasons these Candidates won and lost!” (Capitalization his own.)

#3739. GTA 6 Survey Reveals People Really Want GTA Online, But It Hasn’t Been Confirmed Yet

Grand Theft Auto 6 releases on November 19, and a lot of people are very excited to play some kind of online mode, according to a new study. The only problem is that GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game and has no online mode, at least not one that Rockstar has talked about yet.

Research firm Piper Sandler recently polled 9,000 teenagers, with 90% saying they intend to play GTA Online. It would be shocking if GTA 6 doesn't eventually have an online mode, but the company has not said anything about that.

Product listings for GTA 6 at retailers make it clear that the game is a "single-player experience," so it's not something Rockstar is trying to be coy about.

The poll also found that 40% of respondents said they planned to make additional in-game purchases.

Additionally, the survey found that 70% of respondents who own a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S plan to buy GTA 6. Of those, 55% said they are planning to buy GTA immediately, and 15% said they would wait several months.

Before this, Circana reported that nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6; that's the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured.

Analyst James Callahan reiterated a $290 price target on Take-Two's stock. After getting crushed so far in 2026, Take-Two stock today stands at about $210/share (after a huge rally today, November 4).

It remains to be seen what Rockstar may do with the existing GTA Online for GTA 6 after GTA 6 comes out--whatever the case, gamers are going to be mad.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading starts on November 10, and gamers in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play the game, so maybe pack your bags for New Zealand.

“Happiest Birthday to the Holy Grail …. Love you forever!! Keep being Great,” Corey, 45, wrote to Jenner via Instagram on Thursday, November 5, adding: “You’re the greatest mother , Lovey & Honey to all your kids and im blessed to have you in my life lil wife …..”

“You know, I’ve done that twice, and it didn’t work out so well,” Jenner told pal Ellen DeGeneres at the time. “So I don’t know. You never know.”

DeGeneres, 68, celebrated her longtime friendship with Kris on the Kardashians star’s special day, praising her as “so loving and kind and thoughtful.”

“No matter how busy you are, you always make time for me and anyone else who’s lucky enough to call you a friend,” the former talk show host continued. “I hope you’re being pampered and showered with love. I love you. Happy birthday!”

#3736. GTA 6 Is A Massive Download, But You May Qualify For A Free Speed Boost To Download It Faster

Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and the game's file size, 212GB, is truly massive. One internet company, Spectrum, is turning this into a marketing moment for its own services by offering members a "free Gig Speed Lift" in November to help download the game faster.

Available November 9-30, the offer has "no cost and no strings attached," the company said. The offer is fairly straightforward: Customers with a qualifying internet plan and compatible equipment can use the My Spectrum app to opt in. Then on November 9, customers will have their download speeds upped to 1Gbps. If you're already on a plan offering that, you'll get boosted to 2Gbps.

Spectrum said the boost should allow people to download GTA 6 in under 30 minutes.

The free upgrade offer runs through November 30, so that also covers Thanksgiving, when you might have a bunch of people in your home and want faster internet. It also covers the Black Friday and Cyber Monday shopping holidays.

After November 30, the speed boost gets pulled from your account with no further action required on your part. The whole idea here is that Spectrum thinks you'll enjoy it so much that you'll pay to upgrade on a more permanent basis.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. For more, check out the exact GTA 6 worldwide release times to find out when it unlocks where you live.
